title: SDK adopter psychology and copy notes (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is an intentionally small, messy sketch for how we think about the human side of the SDK first-run experience — the microcopy, the affordances, and the telemetry we need to iterate quickly. Not a final PRD.

Why this matters (one-liner):
Developers decide to continue using an SDK in the first 5–10 minutes. Clear, empathic copy + tiny success moments are exponentially more effective than more docs pages.

Audience and adopter personas (quick):
- Experimenter (early-stage eng at startup): wants a demo in <30 minutes; tolerates rough edges if they can ship fast.
- Integrator (platform/infra eng at mid-market): cares about reliability, reproducible local runs, and telemetry hooks.
- Product builder (PM/engineer at enterprise): needs copy they can hand to non-engineers (legal, ops), cares about security wording.

Core hypotheses to test (prioritized):
1) A single-sentence promise + one runnable command reduces time-to-first-success by 40%.
2) Microcopy that acknowledges failure modes ("If you see X, try Y") reduces support pings by 25%.
3) Instrumenting 6 events (init, auth-success, sample-call, error-500, fallback-used, successlytics-optin) gives actionable signals for the first 1,000 users.

One-sentence promises (short, testable variants):
- "Get a working LLM call in under a minute — no cloud creds required."
- "Embed Redwood calls in your app with one install and one line of code."
- "From local prototype to a production route: scaffolding that grows with you."

Lead-in copy variations for CLI/README top-of-page (pick one per experiment):
- Friendly, urgent: "Quick start: run this and see Redwood respond in 60s."
- Trust-first (enterprise): "Secure calls, clear telemetry, predictable cost — start locally."
- Playground-oriented: "Try examples, tweak prompts, ship a sample in minutes."

First 5 minute checklist (for README + landing page placement):
1) One-liner promise
2) Badging: SDK version + compatibility (node/python/go)
3) Install command (copy/paste single line)
4) Minimal config snippet (highlight required env var only)
5) Runnable example that prints response to stdout
6) Troubleshooting single-line (what to check if it fails)

Microcopy patterns and examples
- Successful call (UI/CLI): "✅ Done — model replied in 80ms. Example: "Here’s a short summary…""
- Timeout: "Request timed out. Try a smaller input or enable streaming to see partial results."
- Auth error: "We couldn't verify your API key. Check REDWOOD_API_KEY, or run: redwood login"
- Rate limit: "You're at the rate limit for your account. Try a lower concurrency or contact support for burst increases."
- Private deploy note: "Using a private control plane? Switch to the VPC guide for keys and routing."

Error messaging design principles
- Be actionable: always pair the error with the next step (command, doc anchor, or fallback).
- Use plain language: avoid internal codes as the primary text (codes ok secondary).
- Surface severity: visually differentiate warnings vs blocking errors.

Telemetry event plan (minimum viable set):
- sdk.init (once per environment): props: sdk_lang, version, node_env
- sdk.auth_attempt (on token/method submission): success boolean
- sdk.sample_call (first successful API call): model, latency_ms, prompt_token_count
- sdk.error (any uncaught sdk error): code, message, stack_hash
- sdk.fallback_used (when SDK automatically falls back to a variant): reason, variant
- sdk.opt_in_metrics (opt-in event to respect privacy)

Event privacy notes: always sample sensitive data; never send full prompts unless user explicitly opts in. Make opt-in explicit in README.

Onboarding flow sketches (3 short flows)
- Flow A: CLI-first (fastest to success)
  1) npm install @redwood/sdk (or pip install redwood)
  2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... (or redwood login)
  3) node ./examples/hello.js (prints a short reply)
  4) Suggest next: "Wire a route with express/fastapi"

- Flow B: Local-sim (no remote creds, demo mode)
  1) repo clone && run ./dev-local.sh
  2) UI opens at localhost:3000 with a Playground and sample prompts
  3) Click "Inspect request" to see headers and telemetry events
  4) Convert demo config to real API key with one button

- Flow C: Enterprise checklist (prep for handoff)
  1) Install and verify SDK in a sandbox tenant
  2) Confirm KMS/HSM key integration docs are reachable
  3) Add SDK telemetry whitelist and share schema with security
  4) Run a smoke test and save trace link for audit

Snippets for README (copy/paste ready)
- Node minimal: 
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  client.generate('Summarize: Roast my README in one sentence').then(console.log)

- Python minimal: 
  from redwood import Redwood
  c = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
  print(c.generate('Summarize this note.'))

Calls-to-action (experiment candidates)
- "Run the example" (primary CTA near top)
- "Try demo mode (no key)" (lower friction)
- "Show my team (copyable snippet)" (shareable KVs)

Telemetry-backed experiments to run in first 8 weeks
- Measure median time from repo open -> sdk.sample_call. Target: <5 minutes for 50% of users.
- Track rate of 'readme-click-to-run' (button click) -> success. If <30%, iterate copy/CTA.
- A/B test two promise lines (speed vs trust) and measure conversion to demo-mode run.

Support & common friction we see (notes from triage):
- Missing env var (most common): ensure the README has exact env var name in big font.
- Confusing error codes: map top 6 to microcopy with next steps.
- Local dev network issues: provide one-liner NAT/Proxy troubleshooting.

Unresolved questions / TODOs
- Should demo mode accept pasted prompts for telemetry sampling? (privacy risk)
- Exact schema for sdk.sample_call: do we include prompt tokens or ranges only?
- Do we surface cost-estimate microcopy ("~0.2¢ per call") in starter README? (will it reduce friction or increase anxiety?)
- Who owns the localized copy variants for non-English docs? Ops or Docs team?

Immediate next actions (this week)
1) Pick 3 one-line promises and wire A/B experiments with the README 'hero' CTA (owner: Diego).
2) Add the 6 telemetry events to the lightweight SDK telemetry shim and gate on opt-in (owner: Sana).
3) Create two microcopy error mappings for the top 3 error codes (owner: Evan).
4) Run a 1-hour hallway test with 3 external engineers to time the first-run flow and capture pain points (owner: Aisha).

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep README under 200 lines. People bail at the 7th example.
- Examples should be copyable in 2 clicks (copy button + run).
- Emphasize "copyable snippet" as a share feature for product managers.

Appendix: raw brainstorm snippets (quick, unpolished)
- Tagline: "Start local. Scale reliably."
- Snackable benefits list: "1) Run locally 2) Hit hosted API 3) Migrate to Dedicated"
- Quick FAQ line: "Do I need a credit card? No — demo mode works out of the box."

End of draft.

Questions welcome — ping me in #devexp or add comments on this doc.
